forecasts.reason: Bit-identical math keeps accuracy; saves about 0.05–0.1 s of trial-0 first-call cost, though some of it may already be absorbed.
The whitening bias already stops at 3 epochs (about 32% of steps), so the idea reduces to moving the cutoff to 20%. The saving is small and the accuracy change is within noise.
A deeper freeze saves about 0.15 s but costs about 0.1–0.2 pp; it is likely to fall just below the keep gate.
Fresh seeds will probably regress toward about 0.7525 because of the winner's curse, so the margin over 0.75 is thin.
Removing the BN passes on large maps should save about 2–3%, but the fold and eval-BN mismatch adds accuracy risk.
A diagnostic with no recipe change; it will probably show the non-GEMM share at 30% or more.
Muon likely contributes a real gain of 0.3 pp or more. Dropping it saves about 3% of time but loses accuracy, so it fails the bar.

cruxes: What is the true held-out (fresh-seed) mean of the E034 tip? If it is below 0.752, further trims are blocked until an accuracy lever is found.
What share of the step is memory-bound (BN/GELU/pool) on the large maps? That sets the value of the remaining freeze, BN-fold and truncation levers.
Does the freeze plus epoch top-up remain a net time gain on the PCIe judge?
